quotes_checked: all quotes read against the server or confirmed as exact substrings: 29 of 29 exact (agreed 4, reading 1 eight, reading 2 eight, reading 3 eight, with the repeated 19:6 and 14:39 counted once per use)

fixes.why: 'Open but cautious' carries a weighted 'but' and 'cautious' is an evaluative word its holders may not own; the _why itself notes it is the owner's phrase. It also sits beside the other labels, which describe a claim, not a temperament.
fixes.fix: Open: the Spirit may give the gift today, and whatever is practised is tested, interpreted and ordered

fixes.why: Isaiah 28:11 differs in wording from Paul's quotation (the writer's own check), so 'stand in Isaiah 28:11-12' overstates. Paul adapts the text, and scholars and literary readers both note this.
fixes.fix: Paul introduces the words as written “in the Law” (the scriptures of Israel); they are taken from Isaiah 28:11-12, where they are addressed to Isaiah's own people, and Paul's wording differs from Isaiah's. Read as foreign speech being a sign to a people who do not listen.

fixes.why: 1 Corinthians 14:18 is among the first verses holders of this reading cite (Paul himself speaks in tongues, and more than the Corinthians), and it shows that Paul's correction in chapter 14 regulates the gift and does not discourage it. The chapter's argument is otherwise shown only from the regulating side.
fixes.fix: Add {"ref": "1 Corinthians 14:18", "quote": "I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.", "note": "Paul's own practice, given thanks for, beside his rules for the church."}

fixes.why: The writer notes that Hebrews 2:3-4 (and Ephesians 2:20, 2 Corinthians 12:12) are what this reading cites first; without Hebrews 2:4 the reading's central claim, that signs confirmed the first preaching, has no verse of its own. Its absence is the largest imbalance, and 2 Corinthians 12:12 is its companion.
fixes.fix: Add {"ref": "Hebrews 2:4", "quote": "and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.", "note": "Read as signs that affirmed the message at its first preaching, as something done for the church's beginning."} and {"ref": "2 Corinthians 12:12", "quote": "The marks of a true apostle-signs, wonders, and miracles-were performed among you with great perseverance.", "note": "Read as signs that marked the apostles."}. Counts then become 9, 10, 8; add 1 Corinthians 14:4 (‘edifies himself’, checked by the writer) to reading 3 or accept the imbalance given the cessationist verses are cited outside chapters 12-14.

fixes.why: 'Read as having changed with the church's age' and 'a purpose that belongs to the church's opening' state the holders' reading, but the answers block says 'an apportioning they read as having changed' without saying the text does not state the change. Since the card's rule is that the text itself is not made to settle the question, the sentence should mark that this is inferred by holders.
fixes.fix: Replace “an apportioning they read as having changed with the church's age” with “an apportioning they take to have changed with the church's age, though no verse states a date.”

fixes.why: The agreed summary rightly lists 12:7, 13:2 and 14:26, but says 'no gift counts for anything without love' where 13:2 says the speaker is 'nothing'; the paraphrase is slightly stronger than the verse and 13:1-3 as a unit (tongues, prophecy, faith, giving) is the argument's hinge.
fixes.fix: Replace “and that no gift counts for anything without love” with “and that, without love, the one who has these gifts is nothing (13:1-3)”.

summary: Every quote is the Berean's exact words, and the card is even-handed in structure, with no verdict and a fair split of the language question across the readings. It needs the Open-reading label de-tilted, the Isaiah 28 note corrected to 'taken from', and the cessationist reading given the verses its holders cite first (Hebrews 2:4, 2 Corinthians 12:12), with 1 Corinthians 14:18 added to the first reading.
